newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC Warburg sees upside potential for Swiss shares.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg sees upside potential for Swiss shares.

text.p: Foreign liquidity inflows should provide upside potential for Swiss equities, with European recovery anxiety and a favourable marco environment supporting sentiment, SBC Warburg said in its Swiss Market Quarterly.
It said earnings momentum should be helped by the base effect from restructuring efforts of 1996 and the improving currency situation.

SBC also said that although the domestic economy is expected to bottom out this year, it is unlikely to exert material influence on market earnings momentum due to the low impact of domestic GDP shifts on the equity market overall.

The report went on to state that, despite the fact that the market looks overvalued on most of SBC Warburg's measures, it saw only limited downside risk due to the weakening of the trade-weighted Swiss franc and the still favourable interest rate environment.
However, on an international valuation basis, most Swiss large cap stocks have caught up ground, which should be a limiting factor for the medium-term upside.

The report further stated that drug stock valuations were still attractive on an international basis. It expected this positive sentiment to persist and it therefore recommended an overweighting on the sector.
It rated the electricals/electronics sector as neutral, but called for maintaining an overweighting in engineering stocks, which it said should benefit most from the currency situation.
Banks were still unattractive on valuation grounds and SBC recommended that investors continue to play the exposure to insurers through Swiss Re.
It also said the valuation of the consumer sector as a whole looked demanding and suggested using it as a source of funds.
